review: Reviewed the complete 71-track inventory, title indexes for AI Plumbers, Containers, Security, Python, Software Performance, Confidential Computing and HPC/Big Data. Sunday-only tracks fall outside this Saturday visit. Read the AI, container and security abstracts; prioritized serving operations over embedded accelerator development, cryptographic migration and application-specific workloads. Fifteen plausible sessions have individual preparation notes. Speaker performance and security claims were not independently tested.

decisions.why: Useful for understanding the local serving interface, but this brief prioritizes operating models over adding modalities.
questions: Where does multimodal preprocessing run relative to the serving process?
Which audio and image workloads should be benchmarked separately for memory pressure?
decisions.preparation: Sketch the current text-only request path and mark where image or audio preprocessing could add a bottleneck.

decisions.why: Connects a local macOS development environment with Linux container tooling, a concrete deployment boundary for this attendee.
decisions.evidence: The latency overhead of API remoting versus the throughput gain from host GPU execution.
questions: How do small-batch latency and sustained throughput change independently across the bridge?
Which host and guest failure modes must an operator distinguish when acceleration stops?
decisions.preparation: Bring a simple host-versus-container comparison matrix. Treat the near-native performance wording as the speaker's claim to examine, not an independently verified result.

decisions.why: A useful lightweight-runtime alternative, but its embedded deployment focus is secondary to running a shared LLM service.
questions: Which model operators or dynamic dimensions still require special treatment at export?
How can an operator detect that a model export changed numerical behavior?
decisions.preparation: Record model formats in the current stack and note which would need a conversion before a tract trial.

decisions.why: Provides a baseline for container observability, although the AI-specific monitoring session is closer to the main goal.
questions: Which resource metrics distinguish GPU-serving issues from ordinary container memory pressure?
How should retention and alert ownership be split between application and platform teams?
decisions.preparation: List the container metrics already available and identify missing request-level inference metrics.

decisions.why: Relevant to the macOS container boundary, but it overlaps the protected lunch and is retained as an alternative.
decisions.evidence: run Linux container images directly on their Mac
questions: Which isolation boundaries differ from a conventional Linux VM on macOS?
What integration work remains for GPU-enabled local inference?
decisions.preparation: Compare the architecture to the API-remoting talk. Consult the official session page for available recording or slides.

decisions.why: Directly addresses the shared-GPU utilization and failure-isolation decisions that make a small local serving setup difficult to operate.
questions: Which failure modes affect only one model versus every tenant on the GPU?
How should video-generation findings be validated before applying them to text inference?
decisions.preparation: Write down GPU model, memory budget and concurrent workloads. Separate the speaker's video-generation setting from the attendee's LLM setting.

decisions.why: An infrastructure-oriented model lifecycle alternative, but its OpenNebula prerequisite adds adoption work for this small local serving brief.
questions: Which parts of the lifecycle require OpenNebula-specific state?
How are model versions and shared-filesystem permissions linked during deployment?
decisions.preparation: Mark which parts of an existing model import/deploy process could transfer without adopting a new infrastructure platform.

decisions.why: Useful for a mixed-vendor GPU fleet, but backend implementation detail is less urgent than service operations.
questions: Which model operations still fall back or remain unsupported on the Vulkan backend?
How would you compare drivers without confounding model quantization or batching?
decisions.preparation: Note target GPU vendors and driver versions before evaluating compatibility claims.

decisions.why: Adds an energy-measurement lens for a local service, but it is an optional deeper measurement topic under the six-session cap.
questions: How should energy per completed request be measured under variable traffic?
Which power-limit experiments preserve acceptable tail latency?
decisions.preparation: Define useful work and latency constraints before comparing energy measurements across serving configurations.

decisions.why: A practical sandboxing option for local binaries; the room-change conflict with the higher-priority serving talk makes it an explicit alternative.
decisions.evidence: Uses TOML profiles instead of code-based rules.
questions: Which filesystem and network permissions would a local inference process need?
How can a policy be exercised before it is applied to a production service?
decisions.preparation: Draft a minimal list of model directories, cache locations and outbound endpoints that the service needs.

decisions.why: Covers request routing, memory movement and fault tolerance, complementing the single-GPU case with a scale-out design.
decisions.evidence: routes requests based on the KV cache hit rate and load
questions: At what workload size does disaggregation justify the extra operational components?
What signals separate cache-routing benefits from extra transfer latency?
decisions.preparation: Draw prefill, decode and KV-cache ownership on one page; capture which mechanisms matter for a small deployment versus a multi-node one.

decisions.why: Connects model artifacts, inference engines and a repeatable deployment lifecycle, directly matching the attendee's operational goal.
decisions.evidence: decoupling the model weights from the inference engine
questions: How are a model artifact and a compatible engine version pinned together?
What rollback behavior is available when weights download correctly but fail at startup?
decisions.preparation: Bring a model inventory with format, size, license and engine requirements. Ask which parts the OCI artifact actually captures.

decisions.why: The mandatory session focuses on experience operating self-hosted LLMs and ties the architecture talks to day-to-day service ownership.
decisions.evidence: What works, what doesn't, and what tooling we still need to build together.
questions: Which operational problem surprised you after the first deployment was already working?
Which load-balancing or recovery pattern would you avoid for a small team?
decisions.preparation: Prepare a failure log template covering symptoms, detection, mitigation and missing tooling. Do not treat a conference abstract as an incident dataset.

decisions.why: Completes the operations agenda with monitoring at the AI layer, beyond generic infrastructure dashboards.
decisions.evidence: security-focused observability for production ML systems
questions: Which proposed detections can be validated without logging sensitive prompts?
How should false positives be assessed before connecting an alert to a response action?
decisions.preparation: List model endpoints, trust boundaries and telemetry retention constraints. Capture candidate detection tests rather than assuming every advertised rule transfers.

decisions.why: A useful hardware-stack survey, but lower priority and incompatible with staying for the AI monitoring session.
decisions.evidence: software stacks that support them on Linux
questions: Which NPU stacks expose a stable interface for production serving?
Which driver and runtime dependencies limit reproducible deployment?
decisions.preparation: Keep as follow-up reading if new accelerator hardware becomes part of the deployment brief.
